title: Installs through cs-npmrevs fail once the build store holds enough npm packages
foundBy: session agent, investigating campaign's failed `make repin` of 2026-09-29

evidence.verified: Against a stand-in server that exits at once, `with-npmrevs.sh` failed in 0.35 s and printed its log. Against one that took 24 s to listen, it waited and ran the command. Campaign's `make repin`, rerun with these scripts against the same unpruned store, moved the `@codesweep-ai/ui` pin and rebuilt the viewer in 31 s. dashboards' tests/test_record_build.py passes 18 of 18 against this record-build.sh, byte for byte, and its prune test fails against the previous copy. Run over a copy of the owner's store, the prune took npm/ from 179 packages (311 MB) to 47 (83 MB), keeping each project's three newest. `node --test scripts/repin-npm.test.mjs`: 18 of 18 pass, and the test for a build whose package is gone fails against the previous repin-npm.mjs.

resolution: `scripts/with-npmrevs.sh` now waits as long as the registry runs, up to a minute, and stops at once if it exits. Each recorded build removes the npm packages of older ones. A project keeps them for its three newest builds recorded within three days, and for its newest whatever its age. Entries, modules and images stay, and a store that is a repository, as a campaign's is, is left whole. `scripts/repin-npm.mjs` passes over a build whose package the store no longer holds.
details: `scripts/with-npmrevs.sh` starts cs-npmrevs and gave it 50 checks, about 10 seconds, to answer. cs-npmrevs reads every package it serves before it listens, and it serves the owner's build store, where nothing removed old npm packages. By 2026-09-29 the store held 179 packages (311 MB), startup took about 9 seconds, and campaign's `make repin` failed with `the registry did not come up`. Each clean `make ci` in lint, ledger or npmrevs adds five more packages, and `npm run ci` in ui adds one.
